items.title: Refactor System Templates to Use Layout Containers
items.description: Refactor all 11 system templates (Classic Light, Classic Dark, Vercel Minimal, Vercel Professional, Vercel Executive, Vercel Modern, Vercel Classic, Dark Noir, Midnight Blue, Carbon Terminal, Obsidian Elegance) from absolute positioning to use layout_container elements with column/row layouts. The visual design must remain identical - only the underlying structure changes to use the container-based layout system.
acceptance_criteria: All 11 system templates use layout_container elements instead of absolute positioning
Column containers are used for vertically stacked sections (header, billing info, tables, footer)
Row containers are used for side-by-side elements (Title+From, BillTo+Dates, Notes+Summary)
Child elements use positionMode: 'relative' with parentId references
Visual output is pixel-perfect identical to original templates
PDF export produces identical output
Table visibility toggles work correctly (work hours show/hide)
Empty containers collapse properly when showWhenEmpty: false
All token interpolation ({{invoice_number}}, etc.) works correctly
Style editor displays containers correctly
steps_to_verify: Generate PDF screenshots of all templates BEFORE refactoring
Refactor Classic Light template first as reference implementation
Compare visual output - must be identical
Refactor remaining 10 templates using same pattern
Test each template: PDF export, visibility toggles, token interpolation
Verify style editor shows containers with proper hierarchy
Screenshot comparison: BEFORE vs AFTER must match

items.title: Restore Original Templates and Add V2 Container-Based Variants
items.description: The container-based template refactor (STYLE-001) introduced rendering issues where elements stack/overlap instead of displaying correctly. Instead of fixing the broken templates, restore the original 11 working templates (absolute positioning) and keep the new container-based templates as separate 'V2' variants for future iteration.
acceptance_criteria: All 11 original templates (absolute positioning) are restored from before commit 9556561
Original templates render correctly in style editor (no stacking/overlapping)
Original templates export to PDF with correct layout
New container-based templates renamed with 'V2' suffix (e.g., 'Classic Light V2')
New V2 template IDs use 'v2' suffix (e.g., 'system-classic-light-v2')
Total of 22 system templates: 11 Classic + 11 V2
steps_to_verify: Retrieve original templates from git: git show 9556561~1:apps/web/src/lib/system-templates.ts
Copy original 11 templates to system-templates.ts
Rename existing container-based templates with 'V2' suffix in name and ID
Open each original template in style editor - verify correct rendering
Export each original template as PDF - verify correct layout
Verify V2 templates are listed separately from originals

items.title: Implement Folder-Based Template Organization with Modal Navigation
items.description: Replace the flat grid of system templates with a folder-based UI. Display two clickable folder cards with folder icons and names below: 'Default Styles Classic' (11 templates without -v2 suffix) and 'Default Styles V2' (11 templates with -v2 suffix). Clicking a folder opens a shadcn Dialog modal popup showing the templates inside that folder.

Folder card displays folder name below the icon
Folder card shows template count badge

Classic folder contains 11 templates (IDs without '-v2' suffix)
V2 folder contains 11 templates (IDs with '-v2' suffix)
StyleFolderContentsDialog component created using shadcn Dialog
Clicking folder opens modal popup showing templates inside
Templates displayed in modal using existing StylePreviewCard component
Selecting template from modal closes dialogs and triggers export
Folder icon changes from Folder to FolderOpen on hover
Existing 'Classic Styles' section (Light/Dark buttons) remains unchanged
Existing 'Custom Styles' section remains unchanged

Create StyleFolderContentsDialog.tsx component in apps/web/src/components/export/
Modify StylePickerDialog.tsx to filter templates by '-v2' suffix

Click 'Default Styles V2' folder - verify modal opens with 11 templates
Select a template from folder modal - verify PDF export works
Verify Classic Styles and Custom Styles sections still function

items.title: Add Full Sizing Modes to Row/Column Containers
items.description: Add all 4 sizing modes (fixed, auto, percentage, fill) to Row and Column container Width and Height properties in the Properties Panel, matching the options available for non-container elements. Currently containers have limited sizing: Width is fixed-only (no mode selector), and Height supports only 3 modes (missing 'fill').
acceptance_criteria: Container Width has mode selector with all 4 options: Fixed, Auto, Percent, Fill
Container Height has mode selector with all 4 options: Fixed, Auto, Percent, Fill
Fixed mode shows numeric input for pixel values
Auto mode shows 'Fits content' helper text
Percentage mode shows percentage input (0-100)
Fill mode shows 'Fill parent' helper text
heightModeSchema includes 'fill' option in template.ts
Layout engine calculateEffectiveWidth() supports widthMode for containers
Layout engine calculateEffectiveHeight() handles 'fill' mode for containers
Predefined Row/Column containers have default widthMode and heightMode values
PDF export renders containers correctly with all sizing modes
steps_to_verify: Open Style Editor at /style-editor
Add a Row container to the canvas
Verify Properties Panel shows Width mode selector with: Fixed, Auto, Percent, Fill
Verify Properties Panel shows Height mode selector with: Fixed, Auto, Percent, Fill
Select Width mode 'Fixed' - verify numeric input appears
Select Width mode 'Auto' - verify 'Fits content' helper text appears
Select Width mode 'Percent' - verify percentage input (0-100) appears
Select Width mode 'Fill' - verify 'Fill parent' helper text appears
Repeat above steps for Height mode
Add a Column container and verify same behavior
Export PDF with containers using different sizing modes - verify correct rendering

items.title: Add Canvas Sizing Mode and Auto-Create Root Container
items.description: Add a new 'canvas' sizing mode that fills the content area (page minus margins) without overflow. Also auto-create a root column container with canvas sizing when creating a new style template. Currently, 100% width/height overflows because it calculates from full page dimensions, not the content area.
acceptance_criteria: New 'canvas' sizing mode added to sizingModeSchema and heightModeSchema
Canvas width = pageWidth - leftMargin - rightMargin (e.g., 595.28 - 40 - 40 = 515.28 for A4)
Canvas height = pageHeight - topMargin - bottomMargin (e.g., 841.89 - 40 - 60 = 741.89 for A4)
Container Width mode selector includes 'Canvas' option
Container Height mode selector includes 'Canvas' option
Canvas mode shows 'Full content width' / 'Full content height' helper text
Layout engine calculateEffectiveWidth() handles 'canvas' mode with margin calculation
Layout engine calculateEffectiveHeight() handles 'canvas' mode with margin calculation
Creating a new style auto-creates a root Column container
Root container has widthMode: 'canvas' and heightMode: 'canvas'
Root container positioned at x=0, y=0
Root container fills content area exactly (no overflow)
PDF export renders canvas-sized containers correctly
steps_to_verify: Open Style Editor at /style-editor
Add a Column container to the canvas
Set Width mode to 'Canvas' - verify 'Full content width' helper text appears
Set Height mode to 'Canvas' - verify 'Full content height' helper text appears
Set position X=0, Y=0
Verify container fills exactly within margin guides (no overflow)
Export PDF - verify container fills content area correctly
Go to /styles page
Click 'Create New Style'
Verify redirected to /style-editor with a root Column container already present
Verify root container has Canvas width and height modes
Verify root container fills the content area exactly

items.title: Unsaved Changes Warning System
items.description: Implement 'unsaved changes' warnings throughout the app to prevent users from accidentally losing work when navigating away from pages with unsaved changes. Create a reusable hook and dialog component that can be applied to Calendar page, Invoice Form, Profile Settings, and Client Manager.
acceptance_criteria: NO FALSE POSITIVES: Visiting a page and leaving WITHOUT changes must NOT trigger warning
Initialization-aware tracking: dirty state captured AFTER all init effects complete
useUnsavedChanges hook created with beforeunload handler and navigation guard
UnsavedChangesDialog component created with Save, Discard, and Cancel actions
Browser refresh/close shows native browser warning when changes exist
In-app navigation shows custom dialog when changes exist
Dialog Save button saves changes then navigates
Dialog Discard button navigates without saving
Dialog Cancel button stays on current page
Calendar page integrated with unsaved changes protection
Invoice Form integrated with unsaved changes protection
Profile Settings page integrated with unsaved changes protection
Client Manager modal close warns about unsaved form data
steps_to_verify: CRITICAL: Open Calendar page, make NO changes, try to leave - verify NO dialog appears
CRITICAL: Open existing invoice Calendar page, make NO changes, try to leave - verify NO dialog
Open Calendar page, modify work hours, try to navigate away - verify dialog appears
On dialog, click Cancel - verify stay on page with changes intact
On dialog, click Discard - verify navigation occurs without saving
On dialog, click Save - verify changes saved then navigation occurs
Modify work hours, refresh browser - verify browser warning appears
Open Invoice Form, make changes, navigate away - verify dialog appears
Open Profile Settings, modify fields, navigate away - verify dialog appears
Open Client Manager, edit a client, close modal without saving - verify warning
Make changes, save successfully, navigate away - verify no warning (no unsaved changes)

items.title: Quick Toggle for Detailed Hours in Invoice List
items.description: Add a Switch component in the invoice list dropdown menu to toggle the 'Show detailed per-day hours breakdown in PDF' setting without navigating to the Calendar page. Users currently must open the Calendar page just to change this PDF display setting.
acceptance_criteria: New menu item added to invoice row DropdownMenu with Switch component
Menu item shows 'Detailed hours in PDF' label with Switch toggle
Switch reflects current showDetailedHours state (on/off)
Toggling Switch updates showDetailedHours field on the invoice
Toast notification confirms the toggle action
Change persists to Convex database immediately
PDF export reflects the updated setting
No page navigation required to change setting
steps_to_verify: Open invoice list at root or folder view
Click dropdown menu (three dots) on any invoice row
Verify menu item 'Detailed hours in PDF' with Switch component appears
Toggle the Switch ON - verify toast notification appears
Export PDF of that invoice - verify detailed hours breakdown appears
Open dropdown again - verify Switch shows ON state
Toggle the Switch OFF - verify toast notification appears
Export PDF - verify only summary hours (no day-by-day breakdown)
Refresh page - verify setting persisted correctly
